record.paper_title: NLS ground states on metric trees: existence results and open questions
record.context_brief: Equality between free and radial ground-state energy levels
record.original_question: For the nonlinear Schrödinger energy on the rooted binary metric tree T_o or unrooted binary metric tree T, does the unrestricted ground-state energy level L_G(μ) equal the radially restricted ground-state energy level L_{G,r}(μ) for the same mass μ, where L_{G,r}(μ) = inf_{u in H^1_{μ,r}(G)} E(u,G) and H^1_{μ,r}(G) consists of the mass-constrained radial functions?

evidence.quote: H^1_{μ,r}(G) := { u ∈ H^1_μ(G) : u is radial } where G = T_o or G = T, and study the minimization problem min_{u∈H^1_{μ,r}(G)} E(u,G), i.e. the ground state problem restricted to radial functions.
L_{G,r}(μ) := inf_{u∈H^1_{μ,r}(G)} E(u,G), μ ≥ 0, and we will call radial ground state (of mass μ) any function u ∈ H^1_{μ,r}(G) that achieves the infimum in (14).

In the light of this, the problem raised in Remark 1.3 would be solved, if one could prove that ground states are in fact radial functions or, at least, that L_G(μ) = L_{G,r}(μ) (note that the inequality ≤ is trivially satisfied).

artifact.category_tag: NLS ground states on metric graphs
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{T}_o$ denote the rooted binary metric tree: a metric graph obtained by taking a root vertex $o$ and attaching, at every generation $n\ge 0$, two outgoing edges of equal length $\ell_n>0$ to each vertex of generation $n$ (so that every non-root vertex has degree $3$ and every edge length depends only on the generation). Let $\mathcal{T}$ denote the unrooted binary metric tree obtained by gluing two copies of $\mathcal{T}_o$ at their roots, so that every vertex has degree $3$. In what follows let $G\in\{\mathcal{T}_o,\mathcal{T}\}$ and assume $\sum_n 2^n \ell_n=\infty$ (so $G$ is non-compact and of infinite total length).

For a function $u:G\to\mathbb{R}$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(G)$ (continuous on $G$ with edgewise weak derivative $u'\in L^2(G)$), and for a fixed exponent $p\in(2,6)$, define the NLS energy
$$E(u,G):=\tfrac12\int_G |u'(x)|^2\,dx-\tfrac1p\int_G |u(x)|^p\,dx.$$
For $\mu\ge 0$ let
$$H^1_\mu(G):=\{u\in H^1(G):\ \|u\|_{L^2(G)}^2=\mu\},$$
and call a function $u\in H^1(G)$ \emph{radial} if its value at any point $x\in G$ depends only on the distance from $x$ to the root (in the unrooted case, distance to the gluing vertex). Set
$$H^1_{\mu,r}(G):=\{u\in H^1_\mu(G):\ u\text{ is radial}\}.$$
Define the free and radial mass-constrained ground state energy levels
$$L_G(\mu):=\inf_{u\in H^1_\mu(G)} E(u,G),\qquad L_{G,r}(\mu):=\inf_{u\in H^1_{\mu,r}(G)} E(u,G).$$
The inequality $L_G(\mu)\le L_{G,r}(\mu)$ is immediate.

Question: Does the equality $L_G(\mu)=L_{G,r}(\mu)$ hold for every $\mu\ge 0$, when $G=\mathcal{T}_o$ or $G=\mathcal{T}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the work introducing this framework; subsequent literature on NLS on metric trees (e.g., later works by Adami, Dovetta, Serra and collaborators on noncompact metric graphs and trees) does not appear to resolve whether the unrestricted and radial ground-state energy levels coincide on binary metric trees. No published proof of equality (or of strict inequality) was found.

status_evidence.title: NLS ground states on metric trees: existence results and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of the paper posing the question of whether ground states on binary metric trees are radial, equivalently whether L_G(μ)=L_{G,r}(μ).
status_evidence.claim: The equality L_G(μ)=L_{G,r}(μ) is raised as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Ground States for the NLS Equation with Combined Nonlinearities on Noncompact Metric Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work on NLS ground states on noncompact metric graphs that does not address the radial-vs-free equality on binary trees.
status_evidence.claim: Later literature does not appear to resolve the equality.
